status: preliminary design-weighted result in DOI+venue-reference frame; high uncertainty; not an all-candidate prevalence estimate
claim: In a fixed stratified sample of 32 arXiv-CS lexical candidates with DOI and journal_reference, arXiv submission year and the cited venue year differ in both directions and sometimes by multiple years. Historical studies must name the target timestamp (first public preprint, venue online-first, or issue/proceedings year) and must not silently substitute arXiv year for publication year.
positive_evidence: Within the 10,779-record eligible frame, 31/32 sampled papers have a source-adjudicated venue year; 14 of those 31 differ from the arXiv year, 17 match, and one paper remains unmatched. A stratified estimate using the reference/issue-year coding is 43.5% (approximate 95% interval 22.8%-64.1%); treating the unmatched paper as discrepant changes it to 44.6%.
Examples where arXiv deposit is later than venue year: 1812.04475 (2018 vs ICSE-NIER 2017), 2309.12169 (2023 vs journal 2022), 2107.14655 (2021 vs journal 2018), and 2506.20010 (2025 vs ICDE 2022).
Examples where arXiv precedes venue year: 1311.0224 (2013 vs journal 2014), 1005.2678 (2010 vs journal 2012), and 1909.11564 (2019 vs journal 2021).
counterevidence: 17 sampled records have matching calendar years under the coded venue-year convention; therefore arXiv-year substitution does not change the year for every record.
For a target explicitly defined as arXiv availability or uptake, arXiv submission date is the correct timestamp; a different venue date is not a labeling error for that target.
falsifiable_test: Expand to a larger topic-by-year stratified sample with known inclusion probabilities and dual adjudication, retaining unmatched and conflicting online-first/issue-year states. Then rerun a frozen historical prediction task using arXiv-date and verified-first-publication-date cutoffs with features frozen before each cutoff. The practical-impact hypothesis is weakened if discrepancy rates are low and the historical results remain stable.
limitations: Estimate applies only to the 10,779 DOI+venue-reference candidates inside an arXiv-only lexical candidate frame, not all 198,690 candidates or all CS literature. The interval is wide; only 8 records were drawn per period. One record is unresolved, and two additional records have date-convention ambiguity (online-first versus issue-year); another has a DOI-title mismatch. Some supporting evidence is institutional or bibliographic rather than publisher-primary. No historical prediction model has yet been rerun.
